BLOCKED: #1015 is still open. Run through `nikaia fmt`, the draft's `main.nika` comes out as a file that no longer parses, so the gate's fmt check (`fmt::every_nika_file`) fails. I committed nothing to `develop`. Report: /home/user/Nikaia/docs/briefs/yaml/y2c-properties.md.report.md

- **Package tests:** the draft applied cleanly and `nikaia check` passes. All 11 package tests pass, including the new `anchors_tags_aliases`. It covers spec examples 2.10, 2.24, 6.23, 6.24, 6.28, 7.1 and 7.2, core tags that fix and check a scalar's kind, empty nodes, properties above block collections, and error cases. I checked each output by hand against YAML 1.2.2.
- **The defect:** `nikaia fmt` rewrites any grammar rule line over 100 columns that holds `if(call(..), "label")`, and the result does not parse. The draft has 9 such lines. The same line under 100 columns formats fine.
- **Why I didn't shorten the lines:** breaking a rule by hand doesn't help either: fmt moves the continuation line to one tab, below the rule's own indentation. Reshaping the rules to fit 100 columns would be writing around a compiler defect, which the rules forbid.
- **Saved work:** the draft plus the new test are on branch `wip/y2c-properties` (b223f972). I restored my files in the shared checkout by name. `nikaia.derived` and `nikaia.lock` in `packages/yaml` were already modified when I started and are untouched.
- **Error positions:** a quoted scalar its tag doesn't fit, such as `!!int "x"`, is reported just after its closing quote. A plain one is reported where the parser read furthest, sometimes the start of the next line. That is how the parser reports errors, not a package defect, and the test comment says so.

Next step: fix #1015, including the one-tab continuation. Then a run can take the wip branch as it is, run fmt and the package checks, and commit with "Part of #928".

The test cache `target/nikaia-project-tests` is at 6.1 GB and the disk has 5.4 GB free; this run created no cache entry over 100 MB.
